newsitem.title: USA: Clinton extends compensation for Gulf War veterans.
newsitem.headline: Clinton extends compensation for Gulf War veterans.

text.p: President Clinton Friday extended the right of thousands of Gulf War veterans to claim disability compensation for illnesses they believe were caused by the the 1991 war to 10 years instead of two.

"Gulf War veterans who became ill as a result of their service should receive the compensation they deserve even if science cannot yet pinpoint the cause of their illnesses," Clinton said at a press conference.
U.S. regulations had required Gulf War veterans to prove within two years of the war that it caused their illnesses but Clinton extended that period to the end of 2001.

Though several major federal studies have found no evidence the war produced a single new Gulf War Syndrome illness, doctors have been unable to diagnose illnesses of several thousand Gulf War veterans.

Many of the veterans' symptoms include fatigue, muscle aches and pains and trouble sleeping but defence and veterans affairs researchers say they have found no patterns in examinations of more than 60,000 Gulf War veterans that would indicate common causes of the illnesses.
Clinton's extension of disability benefits for 10 years rather than two was recommended by Secretary of Veterans Affairs Jesse Brown.

"I have concluded that despite a broad federal research effort, to date there is insufficient information about the nature of these illnesses to justify the current (two-year) limitation," Brown told Clinton in a letter.

Clinton also announced he had issued a directive recommended by his Presidential Advisory Committee on Gulf War Veterans' Illnesses that any lessons learned be used to protect the health of U.S. troops sent to future wars.

Clinton said federal agencies had given him a comprehensive action plan for finding and treating any Gulf War veterans who have illnesses and conducting research to find causes of the unexplained illnesses.

The action plan says there will be studies of many of the up to 20,000 veterans the Defence Department said may have been near an Iraqi weapons dump containing war gas weapons that U.S. military engineers blew up just after the war.
It also says there will be research on stress-related disorders and whether combinations of pills and chemicals Gulf War troops were exposed to could have cause illnesses.
